case.title: Negative quantity accepted in setQuantity — negative cart total enables fraudulent charge
case.summary: Negative quantities (e.g. quantity="-3") were silently accepted by parseQuantity in src/cart/cart.ts because the refactor commit c3fb68f replaced toQuantity() (which guarded quantity < 1) with parseQuantity() (which only checked isFinite). This allowed a PATCH request to set cart item quantity to -3, producing a cart total of -4549.46 INR, which the payment gateway accepted as a fraudulent negative charge. Fix: added `|| value < 0` to the parseQuantity guard condition. All 110 tests pass including 3 new repro tests covering numeric -3, string '-3', and direct parseQuantity calls.

plainSummary.text: The cart allowed setting a product quantity to a negative number, which produced a negative cart total that could be used to fraudulently charge a customer. This happened because the code only checked that the quantity was an integer and greater than zero, but it did not block negative numbers. The code was updated to also reject any quantity less than zero, ensuring the quantity must be a non-negative integer, which prevents the cart total from going negative and stops the fraudulent charge vulnerability.

data.expected: PATCH /api/carts/:id/items/:productId with quantity=-3 should throw InvalidQuantityError (quantity must be a positive integer)
data.actual: Negative quantity -3 is accepted; cart total becomes -4549.46 INR; payment gateway processes a fraudulent negative charge
data.attack_vector: Unauthenticated user sends body {"quantity":"-3"} to PATCH endpoint; parseQuantity only checks isFinite, not > 0

data.assertion: expected function to throw an error, but it didn't

data.author: GegarinSagolsem
data.diff_summary: Replaced toQuantity() (which checked quantity < 1) with parseQuantity() (which only checks isFinite). The sign guard was lost during the refactor.
data.subject: refactor(cart): accept numeric strings for quantities

data.fix: Added `|| value < 0` to parseQuantity's guard condition. Rejects any negative quantity (strings like '-3' or numbers like -3) while still allowing 0 (used by setQuantity to remove a line item).

reasons: Fix is exactly one character change (+`|| value < 0`) to the guard condition in parseQuantity
Both callers (addItem and setQuantity) now correctly reject negative quantities
value < 0 boundary preserves setQuantity(0) → removeItem behavior
Repro test covers all three attack vectors from the log

data.expected: setQuantity with a negative quantity should throw InvalidQuantityError; parseQuantity must reject values <= 0
data.actual: parseQuantity only checks Number.isFinite — negative numbers pass silently; quantity=-3 sets cart itemCount=-3, subtotal=-3897, total=-4549.46, triggering a fraudulent negative payment charge

reasons: Fix is exactly one character change (+`|| value < 0`) to the guard condition in parseQuantity — minimal and targeted
Both callers (addItem and setQuantity) now correctly reject negative quantities
The value < 0 boundary (not < 1) correctly preserves the setQuantity(0) → removeItem behavior

All 110 existing tests pass; no regressions introduced
Culprit commit c3fb68f is correctly identified as the regression point
